title: 1994 AHSME Problem 19
statement: Label one disk “\(1\),” two disks “\(2\),” three disks “\(3\),” \(\ldots,\) fifty disks “\(50\).” Put these \(1+2+3+\cdots+50=1275\) labeled disks in a box. Disks are then drawn from the box at random without replacement. The minimum number of disks that must be drawn to guarantee drawing at least ten disks with the same label is

solutions.text: To avoid ten equal labels, one may draw all \[ 1+2+\cdots+9=45 \] disks with labels below \(10,\) and at most \(9\) from each of the \(41\) labels \(10\) through \(50.\) Thus \(45+9(41)=414\) disks can be drawn without forcing ten alike, and the next draw guarantees them. The minimum is \(415.\) Thus the correct answer is C.
hints: Count the most disks that can be drawn while taking at most nine of each label
All disks labeled \(1\) through \(9\) may be drawn, but only nine of each label \(10\) through \(50\)
